- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. 197b031c orca: bwrap ignores HUP/INT/TERM; re-raise only those deaths
Review round 6. A group-wide HUP or TERM -- closing the terminal of a
foreground `orca-ide serve`, a KillMode=control-group stop -- reached
bwrap too, which died of it and SIGKILLed the payload (--die-with-parent)
before its handler ran: the INT problem again. bwrap now starts with
HUP, INT and TERM ignored; it only relays and exits with its child.

The re-raise took any status over 128 for a signal death, so a plain
exit 148 made the launcher TSTP itself and hang. Only 129/130/143 are
re-raised now; core-dumping signals no longer get a second core.

Tests: the INT-off-a-terminal case failed when the suite ran from a
terminal (the payload shared its foreground group); payloads now run
under setsid. New cases: bwrap's SigIgn has HUP, INT and TERM; a TERM
to the whole group is handled; a plain exit 148 comes back as 148.
The suite passes under a real pty as well as without one.

Also: cat pinned to coreutils like env; the comment says what a
targeted `kill -INT` on a terminal costs; reflowed comments; test
header covers the launcher cases.

Left as nits: a signal arriving before bwrap has forked its child
goes to bwrap (milliseconds per start); traps are set after the `&`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: e8084bc2a822

acab1d5f orca: forward INT off a terminal, survive Ctrl-C on one; GUI dies with its launcher
Review round 5. `trap : INT` swallowed every SIGINT, but the serve
supervisor forwards INT to its child before SIGKILLing it; now INT is
forwarded unless the launcher's process group is the terminal's
foreground group, which Ctrl-C already reaches.

On a terminal, Ctrl-C also reached bwrap, which died of it and
SIGKILLed the payload (--die-with-parent) before its handler ran --
true of the plain exec before this branch too. bwrap now starts with
INT ignored (env --ignore-signal=INT); Node resets inherited
dispositions and Chromium installs its own handler, so the payload
still gets it.

dieWithParent = false is gone: the GUI's bwrap is the forwarding
shell's child now, and that shell outlives `orca-ide open`; dying with
it keeps a SIGKILLed launcher from orphaning Electron.

A signal death is re-raised, so callers see the same status as a plain
exec, and a trap racing the child's exit no longer reports the trap's
status.

Tests: bwrap's own SigIgn (the old SIGINT case could not fail, Node
resets its dispositions), INT forwarded off a terminal, Ctrl-C on a real
pty delivered once and handled (skipped without python3, as in CI), the
GUI's --die-with-parent present and the payload outliving a parent that
spawns it detached.

Comments: macKeybindings uses appimageContents; master's keybindings.json
comment moves onto the activation it describes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: f2105f7d01b2

7db85d00 Merge origin/master into orca-cli-skills
orca.nix conflict: master's Mac keybinding table and activation, this
branch's CLI, skills and orcaGui binding -- unioned, one let, one attrset.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 5b9b4283d7a3

104b3c4f orca: forward TERM/HUP through bwrap, so `orca-ide serve` stops cleanly
Review round 4. bwrap forwards no signals. Under the CLI's
--die-with-parent, a TERM to `orca-ide serve` (systemd's
KillMode=process unit, a plain kill) SIGKILLed the node supervisor
before it could stop its server; with the GUI's dieWithParent = false,
the supervisor's own signals hit the GUI's bwrap and orphaned Electron
serve, which kept the profile lock.

Both launchers -- the CLI's orca-ide and the GUI's inner orca-ide-app --
now run their bwrap in the background and forward TERM and HUP to
bwrap's one child, the sandboxed process. `<&0` and env
--default-signal=INT,QUIT undo what bash does to a background job, so
stdin and Ctrl-C behave as before. Tests: TERM reaches a node-mode
handler inside the sandbox, stdin passes through, SIGINT is not
ignored, and the CLI uses the same launcher.

Also from round 4: the die-with-parent case requires a bwrap script,
and the node-mode case compares stdout only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: de6b0de03076

37db3ccb orca: the GUI outlives the `orca-ide open` that starts it
Review round 3 (Critical). wrapType2 defaults to --die-with-parent, and
every wrapper layer execs the next, so a GUI that `orca-ide open` spawns
detached is a bwrap whose parent is the CLI -- SIGKILLed the moment
`open` returns. dieWithParent = false; a test case holds the launcher
to it.

The node-mode case now checks printed output under a timeout: with the
env var lost on the way it would be a GUI launch, which a running
Orca's single-instance lock answers with exit 0. Comment fixes: AppRun's
--no-sandbox in node mode, appimageContents' users, the header's
description of Orca's own ~/.local/bin symlink. --version matches whole
words.

Not changed (nits): the test's skill list duplicates orcaSkills, so an
addition is not checked; files a skill dir has beyond its manifest are
not flagged; a failed fetch realise shows up as "missing"; README's
test list; an empty /etc/hostname skips the uname -n fallback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 61a8d5ea6654

4e0f5355 orca: keep --ozone-platform out of node mode; tests run under CI
Review round 2. `orca-ide serve` probes ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE with
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, and Node rejected the GUI wrapper's always-on
--ozone-platform=wayland (exit 9), silently dropping the orcad runtime.
The wrapper is hand-written now and adds the flag only outside node mode.

Tests: read /etc/hostname (what CI writes) with uname -n as the fallback
inside Orca's sandbox, in both orca tests; jq instead of python3, which
CI's tool shell lacks, hashing every file the manifest lists; hold
ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE to exactly the profile's nixGL-wrapped GUI; a node-
mode case for the probe above; tighter bwrap and guide-title matches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: af092d532a0c

777a68b5 orca: `orca-ide` is the CLI, the GUI is `orca-ide-app`
Review round 1: Orca's skills tell agents outside an Orca terminal on
Linux to run `orca-ide`, never bare `orca` -- here that started the GUI.
Match upstream's Linux install instead: orca-ide and orca are the CLI,
the GUI wrapper and desktop Exec move to orca-ide-app.

ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE points `orca-ide open` at the nixGL-wrapped GUI;
without it the CLI spawns the raw Electron in its own env, which has no
wayland flag and exits on Hyprland.

The test now also holds the CLI launcher to being bwrap (run from an
Orca terminal it is already inside an FHS env, so a bare wrapper would
pass), runs `skills get` under both names, and checks the skills rev is
the app's own sourceCommit. The rev is in the fetch's store name, so a
rev bump without a hash bump fails instead of reusing the old tree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 253006912444

9e53e6cc orca: install the CLI as `orca` and six of its agent skills
The app's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal (a PATH shim there,
and a ~/.local/bin symlink to a raw store path). Run its CLI script in the
GUI's FHS env as `orca`, so it works from any shell; the skills are stubs
that call `orca skills get`, so they need it.

4:4:  # Run a bwrap launcher in the background and forward TERM, HUP and INT to
5:5:  # the process inside its sandbox. bwrap forwards no signals: under
6:6:  # --die-with-parent a TERM to it SIGKILLs the payload before it can clean
8:8:  # (KillMode=process), the serve supervisor (TERM, HUP and INT, then
9:9:  # SIGKILL) and a plain kill all signal the outermost pid. Without a pid
10:10:  # namespace (buildFHSEnv's default), bwrap's one child is the payload
15:15:  # Signals to the whole group -- Ctrl-C, a terminal hangup, a
16:16:  # KillMode=control-group stop -- reach bwrap as well as the payload, and a
17:17:  # bwrap that died of one would SIGKILL the payload (--die-with-parent)
18:18:  # before its handler ran. (A plain exec had the same problem.) So bwrap
24:24:  # targeted `kill -INT` of a launcher in a terminal's foreground is lost.
29:29:  # dispositions above explicitly. Other signals (QUIT, USR1, ...) kill the
30:30:  # launcher unforwarded, as they killed bwrap before. tests/orca-cli-skills.sh.
31:31:  forwardSignals = target: ''
32:32:    # forward-signals
33:33:    ${pkgs.coreutils}/bin/env --ignore-signal=HUP,INT,TERM --default-signal=QUIT ${target} "$@" <&0 &
42:42:      kill -s "$1" ''${kids:-$child} 2>/dev/null
44:44:    for sig in TERM HUP INT; do trap "fwd $sig" $sig; done
45:45:    # Over 128 is a trap interrupting wait, or the child's own signal death.
47:47:      wait $child; rc=$?
48:48:      [ $rc -gt 128 ] && kill -0 $child 2>/dev/null || break
50:50:    # It may have exited between the trap and kill -0: its saved status wins.
51:51:    if [ $rc -gt 128 ]; then wait $child; r=$?; [ $r -ne 127 ] && rc=$r; fi
52:52:    case $rc in 129|130|143) trap - $((rc - 128)); kill -$((rc - 128)) $$ ;; esac
79:79:    extraPkgs = pkgs: [ pkgs.libsecret ];

commit 197b031cd29e3014738e9fce36fb6e772771d084
Author: Sauyon Lee <git@sjle.co>
Date:   Sat Oct 24 12:12:41 2026 +0000

    orca: bwrap ignores HUP/INT/TERM; re-raise only those deaths
    
    Review round 6. A group-wide HUP or TERM -- closing the terminal of a
    foreground `orca-ide serve`, a KillMode=control-group stop -- reached
    bwrap too, which died of it and SIGKILLed the payload (--die-with-parent)
    before its handler ran: the INT problem again. bwrap now starts with
    HUP, INT and TERM ignored; it only relays and exits with its child.
    
    The re-raise took any status over 128 for a signal death, so a plain
    exit 148 made the launcher TSTP itself and hang. Only 129/130/143 are
    re-raised now; core-dumping signals no longer get a second core.
    
    Tests: the INT-off-a-terminal case failed when the suite ran from a
    terminal (the payload shared its foreground group); payloads now run
    under setsid. New cases: bwrap's SigIgn has HUP, INT and TERM; a TERM
    to the whole group is handled; a plain exit 148 comes back as 148.
    The suite passes under a real pty as well as without one.
    
    Also: cat pinned to coreutils like env; the comment says what a
    targeted `kill -INT` on a terminal costs; reflowed comments; test
    header covers the launcher cases.
    
    Left as nits: a signal arriving before bwrap has forked its child
    goes to bwrap (milliseconds per start); traps are set after the `&`.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Entire-Checkpoint: e8084bc2a822

+  # other statuses over 128 are plain exits (re-raising 148 would TSTP).

-  # Node resets inherited dispositions and Chromium installs its own SIGINT

-  # and SIGQUIT ignored; `<&0` and env --default-signal undo both. Other

# worktree. Closed-source Electron app, not in nixpkgs (nixpkgs' `orca` is
  # the GNOME screen reader), so this packages the official Linux AppImage.
  # The electron-updater feed in each GitHub release, latest-linux.yml, is
  # the source of truth for version + sha512 when bumping: the yml's sha512
  # is the AppImage's, checked against
  # the download with `nix hash to-sri --type sha512 <sha512sum>`.
  # https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/latest-linux.yml
  pname = "orca";
  version = "1.4.238";
  src = pkgs.fetchurl {
    url = "https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/download/v${version}/orca-linux.AppImage";
    hash = "REDACTED/sHSKlfJa4c1O2MCcdJhLrxCVm/NVKT+JtghzxoEsQ==";
  };

  # Wrap the AppImage (not autoPatchelf of the .deb) so the Electron stack
  # runs in appimageTools' FHS env, which works on non-NixOS hosts. Electron
  # safeStorage wants libsecret at runtime.
  orca = pkgs.appimageTools.wrapType2 {
    inherit pname version src;
    extraPkgs = pkgs: [ pkgs.libsecret ];
    # The sandbox gets its own fontconfig, the way every other nix GUI app here
    # gets a nix-generated FONTCONFIG_FILE, instead of the distro's.
    # buildFHSEnv binds the host's /etc/fonts in, assuming NixOS; Arch's conf.d
    # links point into /usr/share/fontconfig, which the sandbox's /usr replaces,
    # so all of them dangled and every family fell to Montserrat Thin. See
    # fontsConf below. tests/sandbox-fonts.sh.
    extraBwrapArgs = [ "--setenv FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf}" ];
    # dieWithParent stays at buildFHSEnv's default: this bwrap's parent is
    # orca-ide-app's forwardSignals shell, which outlives an `orca-ide open`
    # that spawned it, and dying with that shell is what keeps a SIGKILLed
    # launcher (the serve supervisor's last resort) from orphaning Electron.
    #
    # The AppImage ships bin/orca and an orca-ide.desktop. Upstream's Linux
    # install makes `orca-ide` the CLI, and Orca's skills tell agents to run
    # exactly that outside an Orca terminal, so `orca-ide` is orcaCli below
    # and the GUI is `orca-ide-app`, which the desktop Exec and
    # meta.mainProgram use. appimageTools keeps the AppImage's own bin name,
    # so the wrapper is renamed by hand.
    #
    # --ozone-platform=wayland: Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither
    # --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise, and on
    # a Hyprland-only session there is no X server to stat — measured: the
    # bare launch exits 1 with "needs a usable display server", and the
    # explicit wayland switch keeps it running (timeout kill at 20s, exit 124).
    # An env var would work from a shell but not a desktop-file launch, so it
    # is a flag on the command line.
    #
    # The flag lands in extraInstallCommands, not postFixup: wrapType2 is a
    # buildFHSEnv, whose buildCommand short-circuits genericBuild's phase
    # list, so postFixup never runs. The bwrap launcher moves aside to
    # .orca-ide-unwrapped and orca-ide-app becomes a forwardSignals wrapper
    # that prepends the flag and passes "$@" through -- except in node mode:
    # the CLI's `serve` probes ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE (orcaCli below) with
    # ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and a script as argv, and Node rejects the flag
    # ("bad option", exit 9), silently losing the orcad runtime. Node mode
    # still goes through AppRun, which adds --no-sandbox -- just as fatal --
    # if `unshare -Ur` fails in the sandbox; nested user namespaces work on
    # these hosts, so it does not. Hand-written: clearer than makeShellWrapper
    # with a --run early exec.
    extraInstallCommands = ''
      mv $out/bin/orca $out/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped
      cat > $out/bin/orca-ide-app <<'EOF'
      #!${pkgs.runtimeShell}
      if [ -z "''${ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE:-}" ]; then
        set -- --ozone-platform=wayland "$@"
      fi
      ${forwardSignals "${placeholder "out"}/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped"}
      EOF
      chmod +x $out/bin/orca-ide-app
      install -Dm444 ${appimageContents}/orca-ide.desktop \
        $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop
      for size in 16 24 32 48 64 128 256 512; do
        install -Dm444 \
          ${appimageContents}/usr/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png \
          $out/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png
      done
      substituteInPlace $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop \
        --replace-fail 'Exec=AppRun' 'Exec=orca-ide-app'
    '';
    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide-app";
  };
  # Hermetic: nixpkgs' own conf.d (store paths, the full standard alias set),
  # whose 50-user.conf pulls in ~/.config/fontconfig -- home-manager's font
  # dirs, i.e. the nix-profile fonts every other app here uses. Plus DejaVu:
  # Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono" with
  # no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another mono font,
  # so without it the terminal lays a proportional fallback out on a mono grid.
  # Scoped to orca rather than the profile because only orca hardcodes it.
  fontsConf = pkgs.writeText "orca-fonts.conf" ''
    <?xml version="1.0"?>
    <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
    <fontconfig>
      <include ignore_missing="no">${pkgs.fontconfig.out}/etc/fonts/conf.d</include>
      <dir>${pkgs.dejavu_fonts}/share/fonts</dir>
      <cachedir prefix="xdg">fontconfig</cachedir>
    </fontconfig>
  '';
  # Extracted once, shared by the GUI's extraInstallCommands, orcaCli's
  # runScript and macKeybindings; let bindings are recursive, so position
  # does not matter.
  appimageContents = pkgs.appimageTools.extract { inherit pname version src; };

  # nixGL wrap: without it the FHS env resolves GBM/DRI via the NixOS-only
  # /run/opengl-driver path and falls back to software rendering — the
  # same reason parsec gets it.
  orcaGui = config.lib.nixGL.wrap orca;

  # The CLI, as `orca-ide` (what the skills run outside an Orca terminal on
  # Linux) and `orca` (their name for it elsewhere; inside an Orca terminal
  # the app's own shim dir comes first on PATH and wins). Upstream's
  # resources/bin/orca-ide runs the bundled Electron in node mode on
  # out/cli/index.js. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: a
  # shim dir on PATH there, and a ~/.local/bin symlink to a raw store path
  # that runs Electron against the host's libraries. This runs that same
  # script in an FHS env of its own, so it works from any shell. Its own,
  # not the GUI's: wrapType2 pins runScript to appimage-exec.sh, whose
  # AppRun execs the Electron binary and never the CLI script.
  # defaultFhsEnvArgs already carries libsecret.
  #
  # ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE: `orca-ide open` otherwise spawns process.execPath,
  # the raw Electron in this env — no wayland flag, fonts or nixGL, so it
  # exits on a Hyprland-only session. The CLI's launcher honours this
  # override and strips ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE before spawning it; `serve`
  # also runs it in node mode, which orca-ide-app above allows for.
  # tests/orca-cli-skills.sh.
  orcaCli = pkgs.buildFHSEnv (pkgs.appimageTools.defaultFhsEnvArgs // {
    pname = "orca-cli";
    inherit version;
    executableName = "orca-ide";
    runScript = "${appimageContents}/resources/bin/orca-ide";
    extraBwrapArgs = [ "--setenv ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE ${orcaGui}/bin/orca-ide-app" ];
    # bin/orca-ide is buildFHSEnv's bwrap launcher; it moves aside so the
    # name is a forwardSignals wrapper, mainly for `orca-ide serve`.
    extraInstallCommands = ''
      mv $out/bin/orca-ide $out/bin/.orca-ide-bwrap
      cat > $out/bin/orca-ide <<'EOF'
      #!${pkgs.runtimeShell}
      ${forwardSignals "${placeholder "out"}/bin/.orca-ide-bwrap"}
      EOF
      chmod +x $out/bin/orca-ide
      ln -s orca-ide $out/bin/orca

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

THIS="$0"
# http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3190818/
args=("$@")
NUMBER_OF_ARGS="$#"

if [ -z "$APPDIR" ] ; then
  # Find the AppDir. It is the directory that contains AppRun.
  # This assumes that this script resides inside the AppDir or a subdirectory.
  # If this script is run inside an AppImage, then the AppImage runtime likely has already set $APPDIR
  path="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "${THIS}")")"
  while [[ "$path" != "" && ! -e "$path/AppRun" ]]; do
    path=${path%/*}
  done
  APPDIR="$path"
fi

if [ -z "$APPDIR" ] ; then
  echo "ERROR: could not locate the AppDir. Ensure this script is run from within a properly structured AppImage." >&2
  exit 1
fi

export PATH="${APPDIR}:${APPDIR}/usr/sbin${PATH:+:${PATH}}"
export XDG_DATA_DIRS="${APPDIR}/usr/share/${XDG_DATA_DIRS:+:${XDG_DATA_DIRS}}:/usr/share/gnome:/usr/local/share/:/usr/share/"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${APPDIR}/usr/lib${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}}"
export GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR="${APPDIR}/usr/share/glib-2.0/schemas${GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR:+:${GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR}}"

BIN="$APPDIR/orca-ide"

if [ -z "$APPIMAGE_EXIT_AFTER_INSTALL" ] ; then
  trap atexit EXIT
fi

isEulaAccepted=1

HAVE_NO_SANDBOX=0
for arg in "${args[@]}" ; do
  if [ "$arg" = --no-sandbox ] ; then
    HAVE_NO_SANDBOX=1
    break
  fi
done
NO_SANDBOX=()
# Use 'unshare -Ur true' as a heuristic to detect whether user namespaces are available.
# Notes:
#   - When running as root, this check will always succeed even if the sandbox configuration
#     actually relies on unprivileged user namespaces. In practice, Chrome/Electron usually
#     disables or adjusts the sandbox separately when running as root, so this probe is mostly
#     a no-op in that scenario.
#   - On minimal systems (e.g. Alpine or stripped-down containers) 'unshare' may not exist.
#     In that case the shell will return exit code 127 ("command not found"), which will cause
#     us to add '--no-sandbox'. This is an intentional fail-safe: we prefer the app to start
#     without sandboxing rather than crash on startup.
if [ $HAVE_NO_SANDBOX -eq 0 ] && ! unshare -Ur true 2>/dev/null ; then
  NO_SANDBOX=(--no-sandbox)
fi

atexit()
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Why: invoked via ~/.local/bin/orca-ide symlink (from CliInstaller); resolve it
# so APP_DIR points at the real install, not the symlink's parent.
SOURCE="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
while [ -h "$SOURCE" ]; do
	DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
	SOURCE="$(readlink "$SOURCE")"
	[[ $SOURCE != /* ]] && SOURCE="$DIR/$SOURCE"
done
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
RESOURCES_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
APP_DIR="$(cd "$RESOURCES_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"

# Why: Linux executableName is `orca-ide` (avoids Ubuntu GNOME Orca conflict);
# `-f` rejects a same-named directory that `-x` alone would accept.
ELECTRON=""
for candidate in orca-ide orca Orca; do
	if [ -f "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ] && [ -x "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ]; then
		ELECTRON="$APP_DIR/$candidate"
		break
	fi
done

if [ -z "$ELECTRON" ]; then
	echo "Unable to locate the Orca executable next to $RESOURCES_DIR" >&2
	exit 1
fi

# Why: Orca packages the CLI entrypoint outside app.asar so the public shell
# command can execute it directly with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, mirroring the same
# launcher model used on macOS instead of maintaining a separate Node binary.

  # the GNOME screen reader), so this packages the official Linux AppImage.
  # The electron-updater feed in each GitHub release, latest-linux.yml, is
  # the source of truth for version + sha512 when bumping: the yml's sha512
  # is the AppImage's, checked against
  # the download with `nix hash to-sri --type sha512 <sha512sum>`.
  # https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/latest-linux.yml
  pname = "orca";
  version = "1.4.238";
  src = pkgs.fetchurl {
    url = "https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/download/v${version}/orca-linux.AppImage";
    hash = "REDACTED/sHSKlfJa4c1O2MCcdJhLrxCVm/NVKT+JtghzxoEsQ==";
  };

  # runs in appimageTools' FHS env, which works on non-NixOS hosts. Electron
  # safeStorage wants libsecret at runtime.
  orca = pkgs.appimageTools.wrapType2 {
    inherit pname version src;
    extraPkgs = pkgs: [ pkgs.libsecret ];
    # The sandbox gets its own fontconfig, the way every other nix GUI app here
    # gets a nix-generated FONTCONFIG_FILE, instead of the distro's.
    # buildFHSEnv binds the host's /etc/fonts in, assuming NixOS; Arch's conf.d
    # links point into /usr/share/fontconfig, which the sandbox's /usr replaces,
    # so all of them dangled and every family fell to Montserrat Thin. See
    # fontsConf below. tests/sandbox-fonts.sh.
    extraBwrapArgs = [ "--setenv FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf}" ];
    # dieWithParent stays at buildFHSEnv's default: this bwrap's parent is
    # orca-ide-app's forwardSignals shell, which outlives an `orca-ide open`
    # that spawned it, and dying with that shell is what keeps a SIGKILLed
    # launcher (the serve supervisor's last resort) from orphaning Electron.
    #
    # The AppImage ships bin/orca and an orca-ide.desktop. Upstream's Linux
    # install makes `orca-ide` the CLI, and Orca's skills tell agents to run
    # exactly that outside an Orca terminal, so `orca-ide` is orcaCli below
    # and the GUI is `orca-ide-app`, which the desktop Exec and
    # meta.mainProgram use. appimageTools keeps the AppImage's own bin name,
    # so the wrapper is renamed by hand.
    #
    # --ozone-platform=wayland: Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither
    # --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise, and on
    # a Hyprland-only session there is no X server to stat — measured: the
    # bare launch exits 1 with "needs a usable display server", and the
    # explicit wayland switch keeps it running (timeout kill at 20s, exit 124).
    # An env var would work from a shell but not a desktop-file launch, so it
    # is a flag on the command line.
    #
    # The flag lands in extraInstallCommands, not postFixup: wrapType2 is a
    # buildFHSEnv, whose buildCommand short-circuits genericBuild's phase
    # list, so postFixup never runs. The bwrap launcher moves aside to
    # .orca-ide-unwrapped and orca-ide-app becomes a forwardSignals wrapper
    # that prepends the flag and passes "$@" through -- except in node mode:

    # with a --run early exec.

      #!${pkgs.runtimeShell}
      if [ -z "''${ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE:-}" ]; then

  fontsConf = pkgs.writeText "orca-fonts.conf" ''

  # Linux) and `orca` (their name for it elsewhere; inside an Orca terminal
  # the app's own shim dir comes first on PATH and wins). Upstream's

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

THIS="$0"
# http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3190818/
args=("$@")
NUMBER_OF_ARGS="$#"

if [ -z "$APPDIR" ] ; then
  # Find the AppDir. It is the directory that contains AppRun.
  # This assumes that this script resides inside the AppDir or a subdirectory.
  # If this script is run inside an AppImage, then the AppImage runtime likely has already set $APPDIR
  path="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "${THIS}")")"
  while [[ "$path" != "" && ! -e "$path/AppRun" ]]; do
    path=${path%/*}
  done
  APPDIR="$path"
fi

if [ -z "$APPDIR" ] ; then
  echo "ERROR: could not locate the AppDir. Ensure this script is run from within a properly structured AppImage." >&2
  exit 1
fi

export PATH="${APPDIR}:${APPDIR}/usr/sbin${PATH:+:${PATH}}"
export XDG_DATA_DIRS="${APPDIR}/usr/share/${XDG_DATA_DIRS:+:${XDG_DATA_DIRS}}:/usr/share/gnome:/usr/local/share/:/usr/share/"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${APPDIR}/usr/lib${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}}"
export GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR="${APPDIR}/usr/share/glib-2.0/schemas${GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR:+:${GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR}}"

BIN="$APPDIR/orca-ide"

if [ -z "$APPIMAGE_EXIT_AFTER_INSTALL" ] ; then
  trap atexit EXIT
fi

isEulaAccepted=1

HAVE_NO_SANDBOX=0
for arg in "${args[@]}" ; do
  if [ "$arg" = --no-sandbox ] ; then
    HAVE_NO_SANDBOX=1
    break
  fi
done
NO_SANDBOX=()
# Use 'unshare -Ur true' as a heuristic to detect whether user namespaces are available.
# Notes:
#   - When running as root, this check will always succeed even if the sandbox configuration
#     actually relies on unprivileged user namespaces. In practice, Chrome/Electron usually
#     disables or adjusts the sandbox separately when running as root, so this probe is mostly
#     a no-op in that scenario.
#   - On minimal systems (e.g. Alpine or stripped-down containers) 'unshare' may not exist.
#     In that case the shell will return exit code 127 ("command not found"), which will cause
#     us to add '--no-sandbox'. This is an intentional fail-safe: we prefer the app to start
#     without sandboxing rather than crash on startup.
if [ $HAVE_NO_SANDBOX -eq 0 ] && ! unshare -Ur true 2>/dev/null ; then
  NO_SANDBOX=(--no-sandbox)
fi

atexit()
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Why: invoked via ~/.local/bin/orca-ide symlink (from CliInstaller); resolve it
# so APP_DIR points at the real install, not the symlink's parent.
SOURCE="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
while [ -h "$SOURCE" ]; do
	DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
	SOURCE="$(readlink "$SOURCE")"
	[[ $SOURCE != /* ]] && SOURCE="$DIR/$SOURCE"
done
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
RESOURCES_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
APP_DIR="$(cd "$RESOURCES_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"

# Why: Linux executableName is `orca-ide` (avoids Ubuntu GNOME Orca conflict);
# `-f` rejects a same-named directory that `-x` alone would accept.
ELECTRON=""
for candidate in orca-ide orca Orca; do
	if [ -f "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ] && [ -x "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ]; then
		ELECTRON="$APP_DIR/$candidate"
		break
	fi
done

if [ -z "$ELECTRON" ]; then
	echo "Unable to locate the Orca executable next to $RESOURCES_DIR" >&2
	exit 1
fi

# Why: Orca packages the CLI entrypoint outside app.asar so the public shell
# command can execute it directly with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, mirroring the same
# launcher model used on macOS instead of maintaining a separate Node binary.
CLI="$RESOURCES_DIR/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/index.js"

export ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS="${NODE_OPTIONS-}"
export ORCA_NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE="${NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE-}"
unset NODE_OPTIONS
unset NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE

# CLI commands run in Electron's Node mode and must never initialize Chromium.
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 exec "$ELECTRON" "$CLI" "$@"

atexit()
{
  if [ $isEulaAccepted == 1 ] ; then
    if [ $NUMBER_OF_ARGS -eq 0 ] ; then
      exec "$BIN" "${NO_SANDBOX[@]}"
    else
      exec "$BIN" "${NO_SANDBOX[@]}" "${args[@]}"
    fi
  fi
}

error()
{
  if [ -x /usr/bin/zenity ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" zenity --error --text "${1}" 2>/dev/null
  elif [ -x /usr/bin/kdialog ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" kdialog --msgbox "${1}" 2>/dev/null
  elif [ -x /usr/bin/Xdialog ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" Xdialog --msgbox "${1}" 2>/dev/null
  else
    echo "${1}"
  fi
  exit 1
}

yesno()
{
  TITLE=$1
  TEXT=$2
  if [ -x /usr/bin/zenity ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" zenity --question --title="$TITLE" --text="$TEXT" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
  elif [ -x /usr/bin/kdialog ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" kdialog --title "$TITLE" --yesno "$TEXT" || exit 0
  elif [ -x /usr/bin/Xdialog ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" Xdialog --title "$TITLE" --clear --yesno "$TEXT" 10 80 || exit 0
  else
    echo "zenity, kdialog, Xdialog missing. Skipping ${THIS}."
    exit 0
  fi
}

check_dep()
{
  DEP=$1
  if ! command -v "$DEP" &>/dev/null ; then
    echo "$DEP is missing. Skipping ${THIS}."
    exit 0
  fi
}

if [ -z "$APPIMAGE" ] ; then
  APPIMAGE="$APPDIR/AppRun"

fi

commit 197b031cd29e3014738e9fce36fb6e772771d084
Author: Sauyon Lee <git@sjle.co>
Date:   Sat Oct 24 12:12:41 2026 +0000

    orca: bwrap ignores HUP/INT/TERM; re-raise only those deaths
    
    Review round 6. A group-wide HUP or TERM -- closing the terminal of a
    foreground `orca-ide serve`, a KillMode=control-group stop -- reached
    bwrap too, which died of it and SIGKILLed the payload (--die-with-parent)
    before its handler ran: the INT problem again. bwrap now starts with
    HUP, INT and TERM ignored; it only relays and exits with its child.
    
    The re-raise took any status over 128 for a signal death, so a plain
    exit 148 made the launcher TSTP itself and hang. Only 129/130/143 are
    re-raised now; core-dumping signals no longer get a second core.
    
    Tests: the INT-off-a-terminal case failed when the suite ran from a
    terminal (the payload shared its foreground group); payloads now run
    under setsid. New cases: bwrap's SigIgn has HUP, INT and TERM; a TERM
    to the whole group is handled; a plain exit 148 comes back as 148.
    The suite passes under a real pty as well as without one.
    
    Also: cat pinned to coreutils like env; the comment says what a
    targeted `kill -INT` on a terminal costs; reflowed comments; test
    header covers the launcher cases.
    
    Left as nits: a signal arriving before bwrap has forked its child
    goes to bwrap (milliseconds per start); traps are set after the `&`.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Entire-Checkpoint: e8084bc2a822

diff --git a/tests/orca-cli-skills.sh b/tests/orca-cli-skills.sh
index afdf58a0..ca614df6 100755
--- a/tests/orca-cli-skills.sh
+++ b/tests/orca-cli-skills.sh
@@ -2,7 +2,9 @@
 # Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
 # that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
 # Orca terminal, and that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this
-# Orca build expects.
+# Orca build expects. Also its launchers: node mode, signals forwarded into
+# the sandbox (so `orca-ide serve` stops cleanly), Ctrl-C, and a GUI that
+# outlives `orca-ide open`.
 #
 # Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
 # puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
@@ -86,10 +88,12 @@ else fail "orca-ide-app node mode" "${out:-$(tail -1 "$T/node-err")}"; fi
 # it saw. Each payload exits on its own after 20s, so a regression cannot leak
 # it. Started via env --default-signal, as Node's spawn would: a background
 # job of this non-interactive shell would otherwise begin with SIGINT ignored,
-# which bash then cannot trap.
-payload() { # payload <out-file>: node-mode GUI launch reporting TERM and INT
-  ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 env --default-signal=INT "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -e '
-    for (const s of ["SIGTERM", "SIGINT"])
+# which bash then cannot trap. And under setsid: its own session, so no
+# terminal however the suite is run, and its own group ($w), so a signal can
+# go to the whole group. (setsid execs in place: $w is the launcher.)
+payload() { # payload <out-file>: node-mode GUI launch reporting TERM/INT/HUP
+  ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 env --default-signal=INT setsid "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -e '
+    for (const s of ["SIGTERM", "SIGINT", "SIGHUP"])
       process.on(s, () => { console.log("got-" + s); process.exit(0); });
     console.log("ready"); setTimeout(() => process.exit(3), 20000);' >"$1" 2>&1 &
   w=$!
@@ -97,13 +101,15 @@ payload() { # payload <out-file>: node-mode GUI launch reporting TERM and INT
 }
 
 payload "$T/term"
-# While it runs: bwrap ignores SIGINT. A terminal's Ctrl-C goes to the whole
-# foreground group, and a bwrap that died of it would SIGKILL the payload
-# (--die-with-parent) before its own SIGINT handler finished.
+# While it runs: bwrap ignores HUP, INT and TERM. Ctrl-C, a terminal hangup
+# or a KillMode=control-group stop reaches the whole group, and a bwrap that
+# died of one would SIGKILL the payload (--die-with-parent) before its own
+# handler finished.
 bw=$(cat /proc/"$w"/task/*/children 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')
 ign=$(awk '/^SigIgn:/ {print $2}' /proc/"$bw"/status 2>/dev/null)
-if [ -n "$ign" ] && [ $(( 0x$ign & 2 )) -ne 0 ]; then pass "the launcher's bwrap ignores SIGINT"
-else fail "SIGINT" "bwrap ($bw) SigIgn=${ign:-unreadable}"; fi
+mask=$(( (1 << 0) | (1 << 1) | (1 << 14) ))  # HUP, INT, TERM
+if [ -n "$ign" ] && [ $(( 0x$ign & mask )) -eq "$mask" ]; then pass "the launcher's bwrap ignores HUP, INT and TERM"
+else fail "bwrap signals" "bwrap ($bw) SigIgn=${ign:-unreadable}"; fi
 kill -TERM "$w" 2>/dev/null; wait "$w"; rc=$?
 if grep -q got-SIGTERM "$T/term" && [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
   pass "TERM to the GUI launcher reaches the process in the sandbox"
@@ -117,11 +123,25 @@ if grep -q got-SIGINT "$T/int" && [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
   pass "INT to the GUI launcher (no terminal) reaches the process in the sandbox"
 else fail "INT forwarding" "rc=$rc, saw: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$T/int")"; fi
 
+# TERM to the whole group (a terminal's HUP, a control-group stop) reaches
+# bwrap too; it must survive to let the payload's handler run.
+payload "$T/group"
+kill -TERM -- -"$w" 2>/dev/null; wait "$w"; rc=$?
+if grep -q got-SIGTERM "$T/group" && [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
+  pass "TERM to the launcher's whole group lets the payload handle it"
+else fail "group TERM" "rc=$rc, saw: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$T/group")"; fi
+
+# Only HUP/INT/TERM deaths are re-raised: a plain exit above 128 is a status,
+# and re-raising 148 (TSTP) would stop the launcher instead of exiting it.
+ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 timeout 60 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -e 'process.exit(148)' >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
+if [ "$rc" -eq 148 ]; then pass "a plain exit 148 comes back as 148"
+else fail "exit status" "exit 148 came back as $rc"; fi
+
 # Ctrl-C itself, on a real pty: the payload sees exactly one SIGINT and gets
 # to handle it. Needs python3 for the pty, which CI's tool shell lacks.
 if command -v python3 >/dev/null; then
   got=$(timeout 60 python3 -I - "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" <<'EOF'
-import os, pty, select, sys, time
+import os, pty, re, select, sys, time
 pid, fd = pty.fork()
 if pid == 0:
     os.environ["ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE"] = "1"
@@ -129,7 +149,7 @@ if pid == 0:
         'let n = 0; process.on("SIGINT", () => { n++; setTimeout(() => {'
         ' console.log("ints=" + n); process.exit(0); }, 1500); });'
         ' console.log("ready"); setTimeout(() => process.exit(3), 20000);'])
-buf, t = b"", time.time()
+buf = b""
 def read_until(s, secs):
     global buf
     t = time.time()
@@ -138,7 +158,6 @@ def read_until(s, secs):
             if select.select([fd], [], [], 0.5)[0]: buf += os.read(fd, 1024)
         except OSError: break
 read_until(b"ready", 30); os.write(fd, b"\x03"); read_until(b"ints=", 10)
-import re
 m = re.findall(r"ints=\d+", buf.decode(errors="replace"))  # the echoed ^C precedes it
 print(m[-1] if m else "none", os.waitpid(pid, 0)[1])
 EOF

input.message:
Round 7 review of 197b031c (orca.nix, tests/orca-cli-skills.sh). I built nothing and changed nothing. I ran the built launchers in node mode only and killed only processes I had started.

Outputs used: GUI `/nix/store/lh63md48…-orca-1.4.238/bin/orca-ide-app`, CLI `/nix/store/5hwz911j…-orca-cli-1.4.238/bin/orca-ide`.

**Chain as built.** forwarding shell → `env` → bwrap (`--die-with-parent`, no pid namespace) → `container-init` → FHS `/init` (bash: `source /etc/profile; exec …`) → appimage-exec.sh → AppRun → Electron.
- `container-init` is a static C++ binary. Its source is `/nix/store/pxkyam1w…-container-init.cc`: it runs ldconfig through posix_spawn, waits for it, then `execv("/init")`. Because it execs, the comment's claim that "bwrap's one child is the payload, every layer exec'ing the next" holds once startup is over.

**Evidence for your three questions**

**(1) Can bwrap be left running with no way to stop it short of SIGKILL? No, and both get cleaned up.**
- Setup: a node-mode payload that catches TERM and keeps running. SigIgn was bwrap `0x4003` (HUP, INT, TERM) and payload `0x1001000` (PIPE and XFSZ only).
- I sent TERM to the shell, then TERM, HUP and INT straight to bwrap. The payload handled the forwarded TERM once ("got TERM"). The direct signals did nothing, and all three processes stayed up.
- I then SIGKILLed the shell. One second later bwrap and the payload were both gone, so `--die-with-parent` cascades through bwrap to the payload.
- Ways to stop it without SIGKILL still exist: QUIT is set to default in bwrap, and any signal the shell does not trap (QUIT, USR1, ALRM) kills the shell, which brings bwrap down through PDEATHSIG.

**(2) Does anything inherit HUP/TERM ignored in a way that breaks it? Nothing long-lived does. The short-lived startup stage does; see finding 2.**
- **Scripts:** no `trap` in AppRun except `trap atexit EXIT`. There are none in resources/bin/orca-ide, the FHS init or any appimage-exec.sh in the store. Bash's rule that it cannot trap a signal ignored at entry therefore never applies.
- **Node:** the node-mode payload resets everything. The node payload's SigIgn is `0x1001000` (PIPE and XFSZ only). A child it spawned through `child_process` showed SigIgn `0` (libuv sets every signal to default in the child), and npx goes through the same path.
- **Electron GUI (from source, since I could not open the window):** I believe Chromium's `SetupSignalHandlers` sets HUP, INT and TERM back to default, then Electron installs its own handlers. Shells that the pty host spawns come from a Node process that does not ignore HUP or TERM.
  - On the running master-build GUI, the pty-host bash shells show only interactive bash's own ignores (`0x384004`). HUP is not ignored.

**(3) Claims now false:** see finding 1 for orca.nix:25. The commit's nit about a signal arriving before bwrap forks says "milliseconds"; finding 2 shows the real window is about 100–200 ms, and that the signal is now lost rather than killing the process.

**Critical**

None.

**Important**

1. **orca.nix:25 is false for the packaged GUI, so the group-wide TERM/HUP fix does not reach the GUI.** The comment says "A group-wide HUP or TERM arrives twice, which Node and Electron shrug off."
   - In packaged, non-serve mode, Orca's main bundle registers no persistent Node listener for TERM or HUP:
     - `PHr`/`FHr` adds the persistent `process.on` listeners, but it is called only on the serve (headless RPC) path.
     - `nOn` uses `process.once`, and only when `c=r&&!$.isServeMode` with `r=!W.app.isPackaged`, i.e. dev builds only.
   - So the GUI relies on Electron's `GracefulShutdownHandler`. As far as I know from the Electron source, that handler is one-shot: its first action resets the signal to SIG_DFL ("We had one shot at graceful shutdown").
   - When the TERM arrives directly and again from `fwd` a few milliseconds later, the second one kills Electron by default action before `app.quit` finishes.
   - This is exactly the case the commit set out to fix. On logout, systemd stops the GUI's scope (the running GUI is in `app-orca-<pid>.scope` and its launcher bwrap is in a separate `run-p….scope`). A terminal hangup does the same.
   - It is not a regression: before, bwrap died and SIGKILLed Electron. But the stated goal is not met and the comment is wrong.
   - Serve mode is fine: `PHr` keeps the listeners and `Gn` is just `app.quit`.
   - The new "group TERM" test (tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:126-132) cannot catch this: its payload calls `process.exit(0)` on the first signal and is node-mode, not Chromium.
   - Fix: at minimum, correct the comment. A partial mitigation is to have `fwd` skip forwarding when the target's SigCgt no longer has that signal's bit (its one-shot handler has already run). That covers only the order "direct signal first, forwarded second".

2. **A TERM or HUP sent during the first ~100–200 ms of startup is now silently lost.** The commit's nit says "milliseconds per start"; that is understated, and the effect changed from "process dies" to "process keeps running".
   - Every layer between bwrap and Node or Chromium now inherits HUP, INT and TERM ignored: container-init, ldconfig, the /init bash, appimage-exec.sh, AppRun and the orca-ide bash.
   - `fwd` sends to that layer, and a pending signal that is ignored is simply discarded.
   - Measured by sending TERM to the launcher at time d after start:
     - GUI node mode: d=0.05 and d=0.15 gave "ran to completion" with rc=0; d=0.2 and later gave 143.
     - CLI `--version`: d=0.05 gave rc=0, meaning the TERM was lost.
   - At the parent commit only INT was ignored, so TERM in this window killed the bash stage and returned 143.
   - Impact: a stop or restart right after start (systemd, the serve supervisor's `terminateChild`, `timeout`) is dropped. The caller then waits for its SIGKILL fallback: the supervisor's grace period, or systemd's TimeoutStopSec.
   - The odds are low, which makes this borderline Important. I raise it because the premise behind the accepted nit was wrong.
   - Possible fixes:
     - In `fwd`, if `/proc/$kid/status` SigIgn still has the signal's bit, wait briefly and re-send until it clears or the kid changes.
     - Or reset the dispositions as the first step inside the sandbox, e.g. wrap runScript in `env --default-signal=HUP,INT,TERM`. That shrinks the window to container-init plus ldconfig.

**Nits**

3. orca.nix:33: TERM, HUP or INT sent straight to the bwrap pid is now a no-op (verified). Before, it killed bwrap and the payload. Anyone using `pkill bwrap` or a kill targeted at bwrap now needs QUIT or KILL. That is reasonable, but the comment only talks about signalling "the outermost pid".
4. orca.nix:20 says "The payload is unaffected". That is true for Node and Chromium, but not for the pre-exec bash and container-init stages (finding 2). Worth saying "once Node/Chromium starts".
5. orca.nix:52: a plain `process.exit(130)` (the CLI's `interactive-login-interruption.js` maps SIGINT to 130, HUP to 129, TERM to 143) is re-raised as a real signal death. That is only harmless when the launcher's INT disposition is not ignored at entry; when it is ignored, `trap -` leaves it ignored and the code falls through to `exit 130`. Callers see the same status either way, except bash's wait-and-cooperative-exit behaviour around SIGINT.
6. tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:93: "setsid execs in place" holds only because the suite's shell has no job control. In a shell with monitor mode (`set -m` or an interactive run), the background job leads its own process group, so setsid forks and `$w` is no longer the launcher. I saw this from my own monitor-mode shell, where the setsid job exited at once. The comment could state the assumption.

I found nothing else new in tests/sandbox-fonts.sh, the exit-148 case or the 129/130/143 re-raise logic.

2. **A TERM or HUP sent during the first ~100–200 ms of startup is now silently lost.** The commit's nit says "milliseconds per start"; that is understated, and the effect changed from "process dies" to "process keeps running".
   - Every layer between bwrap and Node or Chromium now inherits HUP, INT and TERM ignored: container-init, ldconfig, the /init bash, appimage-exec.sh, AppRun and the orca-ide bash.
   - `fwd` sends to that layer, and a pending signal that is ignored is simply discarded.
   - Measured by sending TERM to the launcher at time d after start:
     - GUI node mode: d=0.05 and d=0.15 gave "ran to completion" with rc=0; d=0.2 and later gave 143.
     - CLI `--version`: d=0.05 gave rc=0, meaning the TERM was lost.
   - At the parent commit only INT was ignored, so TERM in this window killed the bash stage and returned 143.
   - Impact: a stop or restart right after start (systemd, the serve supervisor's `terminateChild`, `timeout`) is dropped. The caller then waits for its SIGKILL fallback: the supervisor's grace period, or systemd's TimeoutStopSec.
   - The odds are low, which makes this borderline Important. I raise it because the premise behind the accepted nit was wrong.
   - Possible fixes:
     - In `fwd`, if `/proc/$kid/status` SigIgn still has the signal's bit, wait briefly and re-send until it clears or the kid changes.
     - Or reset the dispositions as the first step inside the sandbox, e.g. wrap runScript in `env --default-signal=HUP,INT,TERM`. That shrinks the window to container-init plus ldconfig.
